title: Field Ops proxy-shim and short-circuit playbook for mixed-topology regressions
creator: Amira Chen
description: Playbook to enable rapid, low-risk containment when model rollouts cause asymmetric regressions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Focus is on deploying a lightweight 'proxy shim' at the ingress layer to short-circuit affected model variants, route traffic to a safe fallback variant, and coordinate Field Ops + SRE communication and customer-facing messages.
acceptance_criteria: A validated proxy shim image can be deployed to the staging plane and toggled via feature-flag in <15 minutes
Traffic can be short-circuited from a failing variant to the verified fallback with <200ms added latency at 95th percentile
KV cache reconciliation guidance documented and automated drain script (kvcache-drain:v1) exists in GitHub
Runbook steps for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private customers are distinct and tested in a fire-drill
Customer comms template prepared and approved by Product and Legal
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger model rollout to 5% in Hosted and Dedicated with synthetic prompt set used by eval-suite/cli:regression-check
Introduce a controlled prompt injection in the canary forcing a deterministic regression in 30% of requests
Observe split-slice degradation metrics in console per-route latency and hallucination counters
Confirm that standard model variant fallback did not engage due to KV cache sticky routing
investigation_notes: 03/02: Initial triage indicates asymmetric failures: Hosted saw immediate 5xxs while Private customers reported semantic regressions only on long-context prompts
03/03: Tracing showed that KV cache keys persisted across variant transitions for Dedicated pools; kvcache keys include model-variant hash

03/04: Hypothesis: scheduled variant rollout left stale KV entries causing tokenization mismatch on fallback. Reproduced locally using model-swap harness (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sim-model-harness #PR-412)
03/06: Field Ops recommended a short-lived proxy to isolate the failing variant without requiring full reversion; SRE raised concerns about traffic skew during proxy warm-up
mitigation_plan: Build proxy-shim docker image (proxy-shim:v0.3) that intercepts routing decision and applies an immediate route override for flagged tenant slices
Roll proxy-shim to staging; validate routing logic and latency at 10k rps using loadgen (loadgen-suite/job-783)
Deploy to a narrow Dedicated plane slice first (customers on Dedicated with low-impact tags) and observe telemetry for 30 minutes
If stable, enable global route override for Hosted and offer configuration artifact + script to Private customers to apply the same override in their VPC
Parallel: run kvcache-drain:v1 on affected pods to reconcile sticky keys; do not rely solely on cache TTLs
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary drill): deploy proxy-shim to internal staging routing only; run eval set for 60 minutes
Phase 1 (targeted): enable proxy-shim for 2 Dedicated slices and 1 Hosted region; monitor error budget and hallucination metrics
Phase 2 (broad): open fallback routing for all Hosted traffic; publish private deployment instructions to affected Private customers with automation script
Phase 3 (cleanup): after stabilization, run kvcache-drain across planes, remove proxy-shim via feature-flag, and document final state
communication_plan: Internal: PagerDuty incident channel #inc-rolling-regression, daily 09:00 sync until resolved
Field Ops: scripted template to send to affected customers with severity, workaround, ETA, and follow-up timeline
External: customer-facing status page updates at 30-minute cadence while impact >0
Post-resolution: send impacted customers a short postmortem and offer a technical walkthrough with Solutions Engineering
postmortem_actions: Harden model rollout gating: add KV-cache-aware variant handshake to rollout controller
Add automated fire-drill for proxy-shim toggle into the SRE quarterly runbook
Improve console telemetry to surface KV-key stickiness per-tenant
Add an 'immediate fallback' route type to the routing engine with safe concurrency limits
Ship kvcache-drain as a supported tooling package with RBAC controls for Dedicated and Private planes
